title: Cancer: current or history, and metastases
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's cancer as documented at this visit.
note:
Chief Complaint: Evaluation of metastatic progression.

HPI: The patient is an 80-year-old man who presents today for a follow-up evaluation regarding his known prostate cancer. He is currently receiving chemotherapy to manage the malignant neoplasm. During today's visit, he reports increased fatigue and dull discomfort in the upper right quadrant of his abdomen. Imaging and clinical evaluation have confirmed that the cancer is now metastatic to the liver. He reports that his energy levels have decreased significantly since the last treatment cycle. He denies any acute shortness of breath or severe nausea at this time.

Medication List:
- Abiraterape
- Prednisone
- Ondansetron as needed
- Enalapril

Vitals:
BP: 132/84 mmHg
HR: 76 bpm
Temp: 98.6 F
RR: 16 breaths/min
SpO2: 97% on room air

Recent Labs:
Hb: 11.2 g/dL
WBC: 6.4 x 10^3/uL
Platelets: 145 x 10^3/uL
Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL
eGFR: 72 mL/min/1.73m2
ALT: 88 U/L
AST: 92 U/L

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Reports fatigue. Denies fever or chills.
Gastrointestinal: Reports upper abdominal discomfort. Denies changes in bowel habits.
Genitourinary: Denies urinary hesitancy or hematuria.
Musculoskeletal: Denies joint pain.
Neurological: Denies dizziness or confusion.

Social History: Retired engineer. Lives with his wife. Non-smoker. Occasional social drinking.

Family History: Father had hypertension. Mother had type 2 diabetes.

Exam:
General: Well-appearing elderly male in no acute distress.
Abdomen: Soft, non-distended. Mild tenderness noted in the right upper quadrant. No rebound or guarding.
Skin: No new lesions noted.

Assessment:
1. Prostate cancer: The patient is on active treatment for his primary malignancy.
2. Liver metastases: New finding of liver metastasis identified during this evaluation.

Plan:
1. Continue current chemotherapy regimen as scheduled.
2. Order a repeat liver function panel to monitor hepatic status.
3. Discuss supportive care for abdominal discomfort, including a trial of acetaminophen.
4. Follow up in two weeks to monitor tolerance to treatment.

Electronically signed, H. Tanaka, MD, 10/14/2026
explanations: Cancer of the prostate under current treatment is a current malignancy: C61.
Liver metastases: C78.7, secondary malignant neoplasm of liver (HCC 17).

distractors.why: Treatment is still directed at the cancer, so it is current, not history.
Metastasis is coded as a secondary malignancy, even when the primary is history.
The metastases are in the liver, not bone.

hccs.label: Cancer Metastatic to Lung/Liver/Brain/and Other Organs; Acute Myeloid Leukemia Except Promyelocytic
